summary: Registry-driven gating: `KNOWN_PANIC_MODELS` (model by hardware by workload entries with a tier of `panic`, `abort` or `degradation`, `error_classes`, and a `verified_safe_alternative`), `MLX_VERSION_BLOCKLIST`, `MLX_LM_VERSION_BLOCKLIST` and `WORKLOAD_ADVISORIES` feed `authorize_mlx_spawn()`.

facts.text: Registry-driven gating: `KNOWN_PANIC_MODELS` (model by hardware by workload entries with a tier of `panic`, `abort` or `degradation`, `error_classes`, and a `verified_safe_alternative`), `MLX_VERSION_BLOCKLIST`, `MLX_LM_VERSION_BLOCKLIST` and `WORKLOAD_ADVISORIES` feed `authorize_mlx_spawn()`.

`authorize_mlx_spawn()` returns a `SpawnVerdict` and aggregates all blockers in one call: G1 panic cooldown (`evaluate_panic_cooldown`), G2 known-panic-model denylist filtered by GPU family, G3 MLX version blocklist at severity critical or high, G4 workload advisories at tier critical; non-critical workload advisories surface as a soft warning.
Overrides need `override_with_reason` of at least 20 characters and write a JSONL record to `~/.cache/metal-guard/spawn_audit.jsonl`; audit failures never block the spawn.

Prefill exposure: a per-worker cumulative prefill-token tracker (`prefill_exposure_tracker`) feeds an advisory worker-rotation gate (`worker_rotation.should_rotate_worker`) aimed at delayed-trigger panics; `oom_precheck` wraps the prefill allocation math with model dimensions and GPU memory auto-fetched.

Panic scanning (`parse_panic_reports`) reads `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports`, `/var/db/PanicReporter` and `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports`, in both `.panic` and modern `.ips` formats (since 1.1.0).
GPU family detection (`apple_gpu_family`) reads `mx.device_info()` and maps `applegpu_g13` to `g17` prefixes to M1 through M5, so registry entries can be filtered per chip.
It sets `AGX_RELAX_CDM_CTXSTORE_TIMEOUT=1` at import if unset, and records a `ctxstore_timeout` panic class.
A `ResourceTracker` (default cold restart after 4000 inferences) targets the mlx-lm 1185 descriptor leak.

2026-04-10 v0.1.0 to v0.2.x (OOM recovery, size estimator); 04-12 v0.3.0 Metal health probe; 04-13 v0.4.0 hardware auto-config (a 2026-04-12 comment on mlx 3186 already cites v0.4.0, so CHANGELOG dates can lag tags); 04-14 v0.6.0 hardened lock reclaim; 04-16 v0.7.0 R-series defences and nine advisories (R2 `audit_wired_limit` flags overrides above 85% of unified memory, citing mlx-lm 1047); 04-17 v0.8.0 L9 cadence guard; 04-25 v0.9.0 panics 7-11 and a "when metal-guard is not enough" section; 04-27 v0.10.0 L10-L13 promoted and registry made community-curated; 04-28 v0.11.0-v0.11.7 (eight tags in a day, CI hotfixes, `WORKLOAD_ADVISORIES`); 05-02 v0.12.0 spawn gate; 05-18 v0.13.0 package split and drift-audit waves W3-W10; 05-19 v0.21-v0.24 and v1.0.0 stable; v1.1.0 shipped 2026-05-19 14:33 as the GitHub release.
No release after 2026-05-19 appears on the releases page as of 2026-10-04, over four months and spanning macOS 27's release.
The 1.1.0 CHANGELOG heading is dated 2026-05-15, four days before 1.0.0; the GitHub release date (2026-05-19, after v1.0.0) shows the heading date is a typo.

v0.13.0 split a 7,297-line single file into a 17-module package; waves W3-W14 ported features from a private fork and ended with a "de-Harper cleanup sweep"; the registry's panic list is therefore partly vendor-internal production data.
Repository metrics seen: 14 stars, 0 forks.

Advisory contents (v0.19.0, 16 advisories): mlx-lm 1090 (before 0.31.3, global generation stream makes observer-mode thread pools race on Metal), mlx-lm 1256 (0.31.3 and later, thread-local stream fix incomplete), transformers 1011 (5.5.x removed `ReasoningEffort`, breaking Gemma 4 loads via mlx-vlm).

Registry entries beyond the panic model: mlx-lm 0.31.3 flagged high for three concurrent server bugs (1208, 1215, 1206); Qwen3.5-122B-A10B VLM MTP 5-bit abort (M2 Ultra 64K-context prefill command-buffer timeout); Qwen3-Coder-Next-4bit server crash loop (about 420 restarts in 2.5 h); Qwen3.5-9B-4bit M5 Max LoRA first-backward OOM; Kimi K2.5 KV OOM on M3 Ultra; a `silent_corruption` class for VLM checkpoints loaded text-only.
Abort-tier events are counted in `CooldownVerdict.abort_count_24h` for display only; only kernel panics that rebooted the machine drive the cooldown staircase.

The `WORKLOAD_ADVISORIES` entry `lora_with_display_active` (v0.11.6) records the display-contention kill and its workaround (display sleep plus `caffeinate -s`); L7 subprocess isolation is documented as not helping, because the kill is above the process boundary.

The vendor's own notes (v0.9.0) say it "narrows the race windows but does not eliminate panic" for Gemma 4 31B 8-bit, that `--prompt-cache-bytes` and adding RAM to 96 GB do not prevent the panic, and that 26.4.x and a 26.5 beta had not fixed it.
The install path changed: the 2026-04-27 comment on mlx 3267 installs from a git tag ("no PyPI yet"); the README later uses `pip install metal-guard`.
Nothing in the source supports use on macOS 27: no changelog entry, advisory or test names macOS 27 or IOGPUFamily 162.

Value: vendor reports 9 panics per week to zero on an M1 Ultra pipeline (self-reported, no independent test); the shim-based controlled test in mlx 3186 reached zero panics without MetalGuard by removing wiring traffic. The two approaches are not compared head to head.
Does any MetalGuard layer remain useful on macOS 27 and IOGPUFamily 162.x, and is the project maintained after May 2026? Unknown.
Does `authorize_mlx_spawn` block the oMLX 4224 two-engine pattern? It has no concurrency gate; its cross-process lock (L8) covers processes, not threads.
MetalGuard v1.1.0 is the latest GitHub release, published 2026-05-19 14:33, after v1.0.0 "first stable release".
The repository showed 14 stars and 0 forks when fetched on 2026-10-04.
The 1.1.0 CHANGELOG heading is dated 2026-05-15 while 1.0.0 is dated 2026-05-19.

v0.12.0 (2026-05-02) added `authorize_mlx_spawn()` returning a `SpawnVerdict` with four hard gates: G1 panic cooldown, G2 known-panic-model denylist plus GPU family filter, G3 MLX version blocklist at critical or high, G4 workload advisories at critical.
`authorize_mlx_spawn` overrides need `override_with_reason` of at least 20 characters and write a JSONL record to `~/.cache/metal-guard/spawn_audit.jsonl`.

v0.11.6 (2026-04-28) added `WORKLOAD_ADVISORIES` with `lora_with_display_active`, `check_workload_advisory()`, `MLX_LM_VERSION_BLOCKLIST` (mlx-lm 0.31.3 flagged high) and `check_mlx_lm_version_blocked()`.
The v0.11.6 advisory says subprocess isolation does not help the display-contention kill and that the workaround is display sleep plus `caffeinate -s`.
v0.18.0 (2026-05-18) added `oom_precheck`, `prefill_exposure_tracker` and `worker_rotation` (advisory prefill-budget worker rotation).
v0.19.0 brought `check_version_advisories()` to 16 advisories, adding mlx-lm 1090, mlx-lm 1256 and transformers 1011.
v1.1.0 made `parse_panic_reports` scan `/var/db/PanicReporter` and `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports` as well, and read `.ips` kernel-panic reports besides `.panic`.
v0.13.0 split a 7,297-line single-file `metal_guard.py` into a `metal_guard/` package of 17 submodules, and v0.24.0 was a "de-Harper cleanup sweep".
v0.7.0 added `audit_wired_limit()` flagging `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` overrides above 85% of unified memory, citing the mlx-lm maintainer on mlx-lm 1047.
v0.11.0 added `apple_gpu_family()` mapping `applegpu_g13` to `g17` to M1 through M5, and `ResourceTracker(cold_restart_after=4000)` for the mlx-lm 1185 descriptor leak.
`CooldownVerdict.abort_count_24h` is informational and does not influence the exit code; the staircase lockout stays reserved for kernel panics that rebooted the machine.

The v0.9.0 notes say macOS 26.4.x and a 26.5 beta had not fixed the panic, `--prompt-cache-bytes` does not prevent it, adding RAM to 96 GB does not prevent it, and MetalGuard narrows race windows without eliminating panic on one Gemma 4 31B workload.

The registry in v0.11.x lists Qwen3.5-122B-A10B VLM MTP 5-bit, Qwen3-Coder-Next-4bit (about 420 restarts in 2.5 h), Qwen3.5-9B-4bit, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B VLM MTP 8-bit (`silent_corruption`) and kimi-k2.5 as abort or degradation entries.
On 2026-04-27 the vendor told mlx 3267 readers to install from a git tag ("no PyPI yet").
No MetalGuard changelog entry, advisory or test names macOS 27 or IOGPUFamily 162.
MetalGuard's lock covers processes and thread registry, but no gate targets two engine threads submitting concurrently in one process.
